name: Sviatoslav I Destroys the Khazar Khaganate
summary: Prince Sviatoslav I of Kiev campaigns systematically against the Khazar Khaganate, destroying its fortresses along the Don and Volga rivers. In 965 he sacks the Khazar capital Sarkel; by 969 he destroys Itil (the main Khazar city on the Volga delta). The Khazar state, which had protected Rus trade routes and served as a buffer against steppe nomads, collapses, allowing the Pechenegs and later the Cumans to fill the steppe vacuum.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Khazar destruction is one of Sviatoslav's greatest military achievements but has disastrous long-term consequences for Kiev: the Khazars had served as a buffer against Pechenegs and Cumans; their removal exposes the Rus steppe frontier to nomadic raids that drain Kiev's military resources; the disruption of the Volga trade route pushes Rus commerce toward the Dnieper-Constantinople axis
